sources.title: Meta Llama 3 model card
sources.evidence: Original Llama 3 pretrained and instruction-tuned variants: 8B and 70B nominal sizes, text input and text/code output, GQA, 8K context, and April 18, 2024 release. The card distinguishes base models from instruction-tuned models.

sources.title: Introducing Meta Llama 3: The most capable openly available LLM to date
sources.evidence: April 18, 2024 announcement releases pretrained and instruction-fine-tuned 8B/70B models, describes decoder-only Transformers and GQA, and specifies training on 8,192-token sequences. Longer context and multimodality are future goals for later releases.

sources.title: Llama 3 reference model implementation
sources.evidence: Transformer blocks invoke attention and one dense SwiGLU feed-forward network on every layer; there is no expert router. Model dimensions are supplied through ModelArgs, whose defaults alone do not identify the 70B checkpoint.

sources.title: Meta Llama 3 Community License Agreement
sources.evidence: The custom Meta Llama 3 license explicitly covers model weights and permits use, redistribution and modification subject to conditions. Its version release date is April 18, 2024.

sources.title: Original Meta Llama 3 repository README
sources.evidence: Documents released model weights, license-gated downloads, sequence support up to 8192 tokens for all original models, and pretrained models intended for text continuation rather than chat/Q&A fine-tuning. Later Llama 3.1 repository migration is identified separately.

sources.title: Meta-Llama-3-70B official base checkpoint
sources.evidence: Exact base repository is distinct from the Instruct variant and links Llama-3.1-70B as a newer model. Its usage examples target Meta-Llama-3-70B and its original checkpoints. The card contains an apparent copied 8B-Instruct sentence under How to use; that sentence is not used to identify this variant.

sources.title: Meta-Llama-3-70B configuration access attempt
sources.evidence: Unauthenticated request returned HTTP 401 requiring authorized access. No credentials, gate bypass, or weight downloads were attempted; exact parameter accounting is not established.

sources.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models, Table 1
sources.evidence: The exact Llama 3 70B base row marks native tool use absent; original April models are distinguished from later Llama 3.1 and its instruction-tuned tool support.

name.note: Original 70B pretrained base variant; official checkpoint identifier Meta-Llama-3-70B has no Instruct or 3.1 suffix.

developer.note: The original card identifies Meta as developer.

family.note: Catalog family key for original Llama 3, released before Llama 3.1.

release_date.note: Exact release day appears in the original card, dated announcement, and license.

open_weights.note: Meta released downloadable base weights under its custom license, with access approval; this is not a claim of an OSI-approved license.

license.note: Existing label denotes the custom Meta Llama 3 Community License Agreement.

parameters_b.note: 70 billion is the nominal developer-published model size, not an exact learned-parameter count. Exact checkpoint configuration could not be retrieved because it requires authenticated access; no tensor count was inferred from another variant.

active_parameters_b.note: Meta does not separately define or report a per-token active count in these original sources. Dense architecture alone does not justify copying the nominal total into this field.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only Transformer with grouped-query attention. The official implementation executes one feed-forward network per block without expert routing; model-parallel layers do not imply mixture-of-experts.

context_window.note: The original README explicitly supports sequences up to 8192 tokens; the announcement states the same sequence length. Later 3.1 context specifications do not apply.

modalities.note: Official inputs are text and outputs text/code; code is represented as text. No original base-model image or audio modality is documented.

reasoning.note: General reasoning benchmarks and improved reasoning claims do not establish a dedicated native reasoning mode for this base checkpoint; no such mode is documented in the examined original sources.

tool_call.note: Meta explicitly marks native tool use absent for the original Llama 3 70B base model in Table 1. External prompting and downstream fine-tunes do not change that released native capability.

description.value: Original Llama 3 70B pretrained text-generation model with a dense decoder-only Transformer, grouped-query attention, and an 8,192-token context.
description.note: Makes the original base variant explicit and restricts claims to documented architecture and context.

patch.description: Original Llama 3 70B pretrained text-generation model with a dense decoder-only Transformer, grouped-query attention, and an 8,192-token context.
patch.notes: 70B is Meta's nominal model-size label; an exact learned-parameter count was not established. Active parameters are not separately reported. This is the original April 2024 base checkpoint with 8192-token context, distinct from Llama 3.1. A dedicated reasoning mode is not documented. Meta explicitly marks native tool use absent for this exact model in its later comparison table.

Meta comparison of original Llama 3 and 3.1

summary: Confirmed the original Llama 3 70B base identity, nominal 70B total, dense decoder-only/GQA architecture, 8192-token context, April 18, 2024 release, custom license, released weights and text modalities. Added variant-specific description and count qualification. Exact learned count was not established because official configuration access is gated; active count and dedicated reasoning remain null as undisclosed. Parent review added explicit tool_call=false from the exact-model row in Meta's later comparison table.
